title: Maintenance Log and SOP Assistant
summary: A shop-floor assistant that answers technicians' questions from breakdown history, OEM manuals and SOPs, in Hindi or English, with the source page or work order behind every answer.

seo.title: Maintenance Log and SOP Assistant with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI for maintenance teams: digitises breakdown logs and answers questions from OEM manuals, SOPs and work orders in Hindi or English, with sources.

problem.intro: When a press loses hydraulic pressure in the middle of the night shift, the technician on duty needs to know what fixed it last time. That answer usually sits in a handwritten breakdown register, a free-text SAP PM notification or a senior colleague's memory.

pain_points.title: History locked in registers
pain_points.detail: Breakdown logs, PM checklists and why-why analyses are handwritten or typed as free text, so nobody can search them by machine or symptom.

pain_points.title: Manuals nobody reads at the machine
pain_points.detail: OEM manuals for CNCs, presses, compressors and moulding machines are long, in English, and kept in a cupboard or a shared drive.

pain_points.title: Knowledge leaving with people
pain_points.detail: Senior technicians who know each machine's quirks retire or move on, and their experience is not written down.

pain_points.title: Repeat breakdowns
pain_points.detail: Without quick access to past root causes, the same fault gets a temporary fix again and again and MTTR stays high.

solution.overview: We digitise your maintenance history and build an assistant on top of it. Handwritten registers and free-text work orders become structured records of machine, symptom, alarm code, root cause, action and spares used. OEM manuals, SOPs and one-point lessons are indexed by machine. A technician asks by typing or speaking, in Hindi, Hinglish or English, on a phone or shop-floor tablet. The assistant answers only from your approved documents and history, cites the page or work order behind each statement, and says clearly when it finds nothing. Safety steps are quoted word for word from the approved SOP.
capabilities: Digitises handwritten breakdown registers and PM checklists into structured records
Indexes OEM manuals, SOPs, one-point lessons and alarm-code tables by machine
Answers in Hindi, Hinglish or English by text or voice, citing the source page or work order
Finds similar past breakdowns by machine, symptom and alarm code, with root cause and spares used
Quotes lockout-tagout and other safety steps verbatim from the current SOP revision
Drafts work order closure notes and one-point lessons for engineer approval

workflow.title: Digitise history
workflow.detail: Breakdown registers, PM sheets and CMMS exports are read and converted into structured records.

workflow.title: Index documents
workflow.detail: Manuals, SOPs and OPLs are split into sections, tagged by machine and revision, and indexed.

workflow.title: Technician asks
workflow.detail: A technician asks by voice or text, naming the machine or scanning its QR tag.

workflow.title: Retrieve and check sources
workflow.detail: The assistant retrieves matching history and document sections and checks whether they answer the question.

workflow.title: Answer or say not found
workflow.detail: It answers with citations, or states that the sources do not cover the question and suggests whom to call.

workflow.title: Engineer approves new knowledge
workflow.detail: Closure notes and OPLs drafted from the fix go to the maintenance engineer for approval before indexing.

inputs: Handwritten breakdown registers and PM checklists
CMMS or SAP PM notifications and work orders
OEM manuals, alarm-code lists and spare-part catalogues
SOPs, one-point lessons and why-why analyses
Machine list with tags and locations
outputs: Structured breakdown history by machine, symptom and root cause
Similar-incident lists with actions taken and spares used
Draft closure notes and one-point lessons for approval
Log of unanswered questions that shows documentation gaps
human_in_the_loop: Technicians decide what to do at the machine; the assistant only points to what the documents and history say. Maintenance engineers approve digitised records, closure notes and new OPLs before they enter the knowledge base.
integrations: SAP PM, Maximo or another CMMS
Shared drives or DMS holding manuals and SOPs
Microsoft Teams or WhatsApp for access
guardrails: Answers only from indexed, approved sources, with citations
Explicit not-found response instead of a guess
Safety and lockout-tagout steps quoted verbatim from the current SOP
Superseded SOP revisions excluded from answers
Question logs reviewed for wrong or unsafe answers
compliance_notes: Answering only from the current approved revision of each SOP supports document control expectations under ISO 9001.
The assistant does not replace your lockout-tagout procedure or permit-to-work system.

pilot.scope: One machine group, such as the CNC cell or the press shop, with twelve months of breakdown history and the manuals and SOPs for those machines.
deliverables: Digitised breakdown history for the pilot machines
Assistant on tablet or phone in Hindi and English
Evaluation on a question set written by senior technicians
Roll-out plan for other machine groups

what_we_measure.how: Senior technicians grade answers to a prepared question set and to real questions from the floor.
Share of answers whose cited page or work order actually supports the statement.
Structured records checked against the original registers on a sample.
Share of questions the sources could not answer, used to find documentation gaps.

faqs.q: Our logbooks are handwritten in a mix of Hindi and English. Can you read them?
faqs.a: Yes, for most legible handwriting. Entries the system cannot read with confidence are flagged for a maintenance engineer to confirm, and the pilot report shows accuracy on your actual registers.

faqs.q: What stops it from inventing a fix?
faqs.a: It answers only from retrieved documents and history, cites each source, and is designed to say it does not know when the sources do not cover the question. Technicians grade answers during the pilot, and the logs are reviewed.

faqs.q: Can technicians use it in a noisy shop?
faqs.a: Voice works with a headset or a phone held close, and a machine QR tag opens the right context in one tap. In very noisy areas short typed queries are often more reliable, so we test both on the floor.

faqs.q: Does it connect to SAP PM?
faqs.a: It can read notifications and work orders from SAP PM or another CMMS through an export or API, and draft closure notes for engineers to post. It does not create or close work orders on its own.
